source_version: Capella (continuously deployed, no discrete version number)

concepts.label: XDCR (Cross Data Center Replication)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - promoted concept (consolidates the earlier 'capella:xdcr' and 'clusters:xdcr' mints); this page is the first authoritative read of XDCR's own documentation, confirming this batch's hypothesis

concepts.label: Capella project (groups clusters inside an organization)
Intra-cluster XDCR (source and destination bucket on the same cluster)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a topology variant of XDCR itself, not an access-control primitive; first documented on this page

concepts.label: Active-Active XDCR with App Services (Sync Gateway)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a bi-directional replication mode gated on paired versions of Couchbase Server and App Services, with its own metadata mechanism (HLV) and its own mobile flag

concepts.label: XDCR conflict resolution method (Sequence Number | Timestamp)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a per-bucket enum fixed at bucket-creation time that gates whether two buckets can be replication partners at all

concepts.label: XDCR Conflict Logging
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - preserves both conflicting document versions/metadata in designated conflict-log collections, distinct from conflict *resolution* itself

relations.subject: capella:xdcr
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (dependsOnService) - used loosely for a structural containment/scope relationship rather than a service dependency
relations.evidence: The source cluster can be in a different [project](../../projects/projects.md) from the destination cluster.

relations.subject: capella:xdcr
relations.evidence: You cannot [create a replication](manage-xdcr-replications.md#create-replication) between 2 Capella operational clusters that are within 2 different [cloud service providers](../../clouds/cloud-providers.md) (CSPs).

relations.subject: xdcr:active-active-with-app-services
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (availableSince) - recurrence of the known server-version-string-citation anomaly
relations.evidence: Couchbase Server 7.6.6 and App Services 4.0+ support bi-directional (active-active) XDCR replications between clusters that have App Services endpoints linked to their buckets.

relations.subject: xdcr:active-active-with-app-services
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (behavesDifferentlyUnder) - recurrence of the known server-version-string-citation anomaly
relations.evidence: Bi-directional XDCR with App Services versions earlier than 4.0 can cause data corruption. Only use bi-directional replication when both clusters run Server 7.6.6+ and App Services 4.0+.

relations.subject: capella:xdcr
relations.evidence: XDCR provides two types of conflict resolution, based on either sequence number or timestamp, whereby conflicted data can be saved consistently on source and target.

relations.subject: xdcr:conflict-logging
relations.evidence: Conflict logging allows you to preserve both document versions and their associated metadata by storing them in designated conflict log collections.

notable_absence.finding: This overview page never once mentions a role, privilege, or credential type - it is entirely about replication topology, direction, filtering, and conflict handling. It defers all access-control content to Manage Replications and Manage Replication Security (see those two files' relations). This confirms the batch hypothesis directly: XDCR's OWN conceptual documentation introduces zero new identity/access-control vocabulary of its own.

cross_component_finding: Directly answers this batch's hypothesis: reading XDCR's own docs for the first time shows it does NOT define a distinct access-control model comparable to Sync Gateway's channel model or the Java SDK's transaction layer. What IS genuinely new here is topology and conflict-handling vocabulary (intra-cluster XDCR, conflict resolution method, conflict logging, Active-Active with App Services/HLV) - none of it identity- or authorization-shaped. See manage-xdcr-security.json for the definitive answer on the access-control axis specifically.
cross_product_finding: Active-Active XDCR with App Services is the clearest example in this batch of a genuine cross-product coupling: Capella's XDCR page defers its bi-directional/mobile-flag/HLV behavior entirely to the Couchbase Server documentation (xdcr-active-active-sgw.md) and gates it on a paired Server-version/App-Services-version compatibility matrix (7.6.6+ / 4.0+) - the second recurrence in this batch of the known server-version-string-citation anomaly.
